set.body:
The type-level half of the tractatus section 2. The runtime half is done: causality and compact support are enforced once in Hrf.apply, so no kernel can respond before its event.

What is left is that a lag and an absolute time still share one type. Regressor.evalLoop computes Seconds(g.value - onset.value) and feeds it to hrf(...); nothing in the types says that argument is a displacement rather than a point on a run clock, so passing an absolute onset where a lag is expected typechecks.

Proposal: opaque type Lag with Seconds - Seconds = Lag, Hrf.at(lag: Lag), and conversion confined to the boundary. Mechanical but touches most of the module (HrfFunctions shape fns, Evaluate, Decorators, Deriv, Regressor, LwuBasis, Toeplitz).

Blast radius is small: nothing outside modules/hrf implements Hrf, and exactly one external call site evaluates a kernel pointwise (design HrfGeneratorsSuite).

Context: docs/plans/hrf-hardening.md sections 4 and 7.
set.title: RFE: opaque Lag type distinct from Seconds in hrf
